name: date format
probe_task: Write a one-line reminder that the Q2 planning review is on the 9th of June 2027.

levels.statement: When you write dates for me, write them like March 14, 2027.
When you write dates for me, write them as 2027-03-14.
When you write dates for me, write them as 14.03.2027.
When you write dates for me, write them as 2027/14/03, that is year, day, month.

name: temperature unit
probe_task: What's a comfortable temperature to set an office thermostat to? Answer in one sentence.

levels.statement: When you mention temperatures, use Celsius.
When you mention temperatures, use Fahrenheit.
When you mention temperatures, use Kelvin.

name: time format
probe_task: In one sentence, tell me what time a meeting that starts at half past three in the afternoon begins.

levels.statement: Write times in 12-hour format, like 2:30 p.m.
Write times in 24-hour format, like 14:30.
Write times as four digits followed by 'hours', like 1430 hours.

name: opening
probe_task: Remind me in one sentence to send the budget file.

levels.statement: Don't bother with greetings, just answer.
Start every reply with 'Hi Sam,'.
Start every reply with the word 'Righto.'

name: sign-off
probe_task: Remind me in one sentence to book the meeting room.

levels.statement: No sign-off needed at the end of your replies.
End every reply with '— Atlas'.
End every reply with 'Over and out.'

name: lists
probe_task: List three steps to set up a new laptop for work.

levels.statement: Bullet points are fine when you list things.
Never use bullet points or numbered lists; write in plain paragraphs.
When you list things, number them with Roman numerals: I., II., III.

name: python naming
probe_task: Write a short Python function that returns the total price of items in a cart, given a list of prices and a tax rate.

levels.statement: In Python code, use snake_case names.
In Python code, use camelCase for variable and function names.
In Python code, write every variable name in ALL_CAPS.

name: indentation
probe_task: Write a short Python function that checks whether a number is prime.

levels.statement: Indent code with 4 spaces.
Indent code with 2 spaces.
Indent code with tabs, never spaces.

name: money format
probe_task: In one sentence, tell me the total of two invoices, one for 1,250 dollars and one for 3,400.75 dollars.

levels.statement: Format money like $1,200.50.
Format money with a period for thousands and a comma for decimals, like 1.200,50.
Format money as USD 1200.50, with no thousands separator.

name: spelling
probe_task: In one sentence, ask the design team to tidy up the shared folders and pick a hue for each project.

levels.statement: Use American spelling.
Use British spelling, like 'colour' and 'organise'.

name: address
probe_task: Remind me in one sentence to send the budget file.

levels.statement: No need to use my name.
Address me as Dr. Lin.
Address me as Captain.

name: dashes
probe_task: Write two sentences describing the release plan for Friday, with one aside in the middle of a sentence.

levels.statement: Em dashes are fine.
Never use em dashes.
Use a double hyphen ' -- ' wherever you would use a dash.

name: length
probe_task: Explain why version control is useful.

levels.statement: Answer as long as needed.
Keep every answer to at most two sentences.
Always answer in exactly three sentences, no more and no less.

name: emoji
probe_task: Remind me in one sentence to water the office plants.

levels.statement: Don't use emoji.
End every reply with one emoji.
Put the 🦉 emoji at the start of every reply.

name: case
probe_task: In two sentences, tell me why backups matter.

levels.statement: Use normal capitalization.
Write everything in lowercase, including the first word of each sentence.

name: summary line
probe_task: In a short paragraph, explain why we should write tests before refactoring.

levels.statement: No summary line needed.
Start every longer answer with a line that begins 'TL;DR:'.
End every longer answer with a line that begins 'Bottom line:'.

name: numbers
probe_task: In one sentence, tell me how many days are in a week and how many primary colors there are.

levels.statement: Write numbers as digits.
Spell out every number under one hundred in words.
Write all numbers as Roman numerals.

name: quotes
probe_task: In one sentence, explain what the error message File not found means, and quote the message.

levels.statement: Use double quotation marks.
Use single quotation marks.
Use guillemets for quotations, like «this».

name: oxford comma
probe_task: In one sentence, list the three primary colors of paint.

levels.statement: Use the Oxford comma.
Never use the Oxford comma.

name: product name
probe_task: In one sentence, tell a customer that our product now supports offline mode.

levels.statement: Call our product 'the Veltrix app'.
Always call our product 'Veltrix One', never 'the app'.
Always call our product 'VX1'.
